data_origin: Own controlled local model of two benign plant-community biomass deviations around a positive equilibrium. The four weighted vectors in the CSV are a CUBATURE REPRESENTATION of exact specified stationary first and second moments. They are not four IID observations, full stationary probability atoms or observed time trajectories. Use them only to reconstruct moments. The declared Gaussian fluctuation model below has those moments; its entire distribution is not replaced by the four nodes. Rounded square-root coordinates are input reporting precision, not unspecified biological sampling noise.
model: Dimensionless small deviations x=(x1,x2) follow the Ito linear model dx=J*x*dt+sqrt(Q)*dW with known Q=I_2 per model time unit. This is a local fluctuation approximation, not a globally nonnegative population process or a nonlinear extinction model. Rows of J index affected species, columns index the perturbing species: J12 is species2 on species1. No detailed balance, reciprocal interaction, normality or diagonal J assumption is supplied. The noise convention is exactly Q, so stationary covariance C satisfies J*C+C*J^T+Q=0; diffusion in the Fokker-Planck operator would instead be Q/2.
admissible_prior: Require a single real2x2J with negative diagonal entries and the exact supplied stationary covariance/noise. Define its probability-current coordinate w=((J*C-C*J^T)[1,2])/2, using one-based matrix indices. Prior scientific calibration bounds w in[-0.60,0.60]. Derive the full permitted family from the moment identity rather than silently setting w=0. This prior class is used for the pre-probe robust intervention even though the separate time-resolved probe later identifies one member.
probe: A calibrated follow-up measures L(h)=E[x(t+h)*x(t)^T] for positive h and reports the one-sided derivative L'(0+)[1,2]=0.55. Time order and matrix orientation are part of the data; the reversed covariance transpose has a different entry. This is an exact model readout, not a finite noisy estimate.
reactivity_and_peak: Euclidean reactivity R(J)=lambda_max((J+J^T)/2), the maximum initial growth rate of log||x||_2 under deterministic dx/dt=Jx. Peak squared-norm amplification Gmax=max_(t>=0)||exp(Jt)||_2^2, where the norm is the largest singular value and the initial perturbation is optimized independently for each t. These are not spectral abscissa, componentwise gain, stationary variance or a noise-driven mean square. The t=0 boundary is permitted; at a marginal nonpositive-reactivity threshold, amplification strictly above1 must be justified rather than inferred from zero derivative.
press_design: Before the lag probe, choose a fixed normalized infinitesimal press direction u=(u1,u2) with u_i>=0 and u1+u2=1. With dx/dt=Jx+epsilon*u, the equilibrium displacement per epsilon is delta(w,u)=-J(w)^(-1)u. Require BOTH delta1>=0 and delta2>=0 for EVERY prior w in[-0.60,0.60]. Among such robustly nonharmful choices, maximize min_w delta1(w,u). The same u must work for every prior law; do not choose a different u after learning w or substitute the selected probe model. The press is infinitesimal, so linear local response rather than finite harvesting or nonlinear equilibrium is the estimand.
questions: Reconstruct the exact stationary mean and population covariance from every weighted source node, and compute descriptive Pearson correlation. A software correlation p-value has no inferential meaning for this deterministic moment representation. Solve the full Lyapunov constraint and prior bounds; retain an explicit one-parameter J(w), verify all negative diagonals, and prove that EVERY permitted J is asymptotically stable. State which interaction signs are actually identified by the positive stationary correlation.

Derive reactivity over the entire prior family and the exact critical absolute w for strictly positive reactivity. Check its equality boundary and decide whether a nonreactive covariance-whitened norm would imply a nonreactive Euclidean norm. Keep the correct norm transformations and a Lyapunov stability certificate in the trajectory.

Use the actual oriented lag derivative to identify the selected J and its two off-diagonal interaction signs. Report its Euclidean reactivity, global Gmax and the earliest maximizing time. Prove that the peak is globally attained and that no later peak or t=infinity limit was overlooked; a time grid or locally optimized point alone is insufficient. A closed2x2 product/singular-value identity, a globally verified derivative equation and all boundaries are possible routes.

For the separate PRE-PROBE robust press design, give the full interval of u1 for which both responses are nonnegative at every prior w. Derive the unique maximin allocation [u1,u2], its sharp worst-case delta1 and the complete set of attaining w values. Keep the full continuous uncertainty argument and the original response equations in the trajectory. Demonstrate why a press aimed at one species alone can have an adverse response in the other despite positive stationary correlation.

interpretation_proposals.A: Positive stationary correlation alone need not identify either directional interaction sign when non-equilibrium circulation remains unidentified.
interpretation_proposals.B: The stationary Lyapunov equation forces the probability current to vanish whenever Q is diagonal.
interpretation_proposals.C: All permitted drifts can be asymptotically stable while some amplify Euclidean perturbations transiently.
interpretation_proposals.D: Making covariance-whitened energy decay makes Euclidean reactivity nonpositive in the original coordinates automatically.
interpretation_proposals.E: The sign of an oriented lag-covariance derivative can resolve information absent from the equal-time covariance.
interpretation_proposals.F: A zero reactivity value at the threshold proves amplification strictly greater than1.
interpretation_proposals.G: Robust press design requires one allocation and valid response inequalities for the entire prior interval, even if a later probe identifies a favorable model.
interpretation_proposals.H: A Gaussian local biomass-fluctuation model establishes a global finite-population extinction probability.

methodological_source.authors: Michael G. Neubert and Hal Caswell
methodological_source.title: Alternatives to Resilience for Measuring the Responses of Ecological Systems to Perturbations
methodological_source.role: Primary context for reactivity, peak amplification and its timing as distinct local ecological response measures. The moment cubature, covariance-current inverse family, lag readout and robust press problem here are own controlled constructions, not observations or numerical examples copied from the paper.
